text: ok because the last question i had is, if you semantically name them, does that make it any step closer to where say i have a prop viewer, i can isolate a piece of it, modify its size/color whatever and it can be stored, or is there still a gap like in the values, as a lot of the numbers feel 'magic'
resolution: Answered the prop-authoring design question. Semantic part names are a real first step toward a prop viewer because they create stable selectable part IDs, but they are not sufficient by themselves; the magic numbers also need to move into editable recipe fields with units, constraints, defaults, and persisted overrides that compile back to the same primitive rows. No code changed.
